# Courier Audit: False `@generated` Headers in the Skinny Tree

## Scope

This audit identifies every file in both the skinny proving tree
(`skinny/`) and the full totality tree (`crates/`) that carries an
`@generated` header but is not an output of any regen pipeline command.
The governing precept is `clean-regen-discipline`: generated files are
always the output of a fresh regen; hand-patched or hand-authored source
files never carry `@generated` headers. A false header misdirects any
reader or tooling: the output looks regeneratable when it is not, and
the source looks protected when it must be edited.

---

## Census Method

`rg -l "@generated"` was executed across both trees, scoped to `*.rs`
files and excluding `target/`. The resulting list was cross-checked
against:

1. The skinny xtask regen targets in
   `skinny/xtask/src/main.rs` + `skinny/xtask/src/regen.rs`:
   `regen-json`, `regen-sheets`, `regen-css`, `regen-real-typed`.
2. The runtime generator at
   `skinny/crates/codegen/src/runtime_generator.rs` (the `emit_sink_only`,
   `emit_general_descent`, and `emit_scan` branches).
3. The full-tree xtask targets in `xtask/src/main.rs`:
   `regen-css`, `regen-json`, `regen-math`, `regen-csv`, `regen-bbnf`,
   `regen-bnf`, `regen-ebnf`, `regen-css-pretty`, `regen-google-sheets`.

Files whose `@generated` content appeared only as a string literal
inside an emitter (e.g., `codegen/src/lib.rs:99`,
`json_typed_direct.rs:14`, `lock14_baseline.rs:402`) were classified as
clean: the marker is carried in generated output, not asserted on the
source file itself.

---

## Full-Tree (`crates/`) Verdict

Every `@generated` file found in `crates/core/src/runtime/` is a
genuine regen pipeline output. Each carries a grammar-specific header
(`// @generated by xtask regen-json; do not edit by hand.`, etc.) that
matches one of the nine registered xtask commands. The file
`crates/ir/build.rs` contains `@generated` only as a string literal it
emits into `$OUT_DIR/production_manifest_table.rs`; the build script
itself is not labeled generated. No violations in the full tree.

---

## Skinny-Tree Violations

### Primary Cluster: `skinny/crates/codegen/src/json_templates/`

Four hand-authored source files carry `@generated` headers:

**`json_templates/value.rs` (172 lines) — line 1**

Content: `JsonNodeKind` enum (discriminant matched on structural bytes),
`JsonValue<'doc, 'input>`, `JsonToken`, `ParseError`, `ParseErrorKind`,
and `value_from_ref`. These are hand-authored and have received multiple
commits spanning SK-V3 through SK-V18. The file is included into the
regen pipeline via:

```rust
"value.rs" => include_str!("json_templates/value.rs").to_string(),
// runtime_generator.rs:122
```

The file is passed through raw (no `normalize()` call). The `@generated`
header in the template is the only source of the `@generated` header in
the output `runtime/src/grammars/json/value.rs`. No regen command
re-derives this file from the grammar; editing the template
is the only route.

**`json_templates/view.rs` (488 lines) — line 1**

Content: `JsonRoot`, `JsonDocument`, `JsonObject`, `JsonArray`,
`JsonPair`, `JsonString`, `JsonNumber`, `JsonBool`, `JsonNull` — the
entire tape-backed view layer. Also raw-copied:

```rust
"view.rs" => include_str!("json_templates/view.rs").to_string(),
// runtime_generator.rs:126
```

This is the largest hand-authored template and the furthest from
machine-derivability in its current form. No regen command touches it.

**`json_templates/generated.rs` (391 lines) — line 1**

Content: structural descent parser preamble — `parse_json`,
`parse_value`, `parse_value_at`, `dispatch_value`, `parse_object`,
`parse_pair`, `parse_key_colon`, `parse_array`, `parse_string`,
`match_tiny_plain_string`, `match_number_at_digit`, `parse_literal`,
`skip_ws`, `consume_delimiter`, `consume_quote_at_cursor`, and six more
utilities. These implement the tape-retained path. The file is also
raw-copied and the `json_sink_direct::render()` output is appended to
it. The boundary falls at line 391 of the output `generated.rs`; lines
392–960 are grammar-derived. The 391-line preamble is hand-authored and
carries a false `@generated` header.

**`json_templates/parser.rs` (69 lines) — line 1**

Content: `ParserState<'i>` struct (input, bytes, cursor, tape) and its
`new()` constructor. Raw-copied; `JSON_PARSE_ONLY_PARSER_RS` appended
afterwards. No regen derivation path exists for this file.

---

### Non-Violations Confirmed

`json_templates/visitor.rs` (38 lines): no `@generated` header. It is
routed through `normalize()` which prepends the header before writing
the output:

```rust
"visitor.rs" => normalize(include_str!("json_templates/visitor.rs")),
// runtime_generator.rs:130
```

`json_templates/config.rs` (19 lines): no `@generated` header. Also
routed through `normalize()` via `render_json_config()`:

```rust
let mut out = normalize(include_str!("json_templates/config.rs"));
// runtime_generator.rs:281
```

These two files represent the correct pattern: the template carries no
header; `normalize()` adds one at emission time.

---

### The Structural Asymmetry

The `emit_sink_only` branch in `runtime_generator.rs` produces two
functionally distinct halves of the output `generated.rs`:

- **Lines 1–391** (tape-retained path): from `json_templates/generated.rs`,
  hand-authored, falsely marked `@generated`.
- **Lines 392–960** (sink-direct path): from `json_sink_direct::render()`,
  grammar-derived via a walk over the `SinkOnlyProgram` IR.

The CSS path (`emit_scan`) has no equivalent split: its entire
`generated.rs` output is derived from `css_scan_direct::render()`. The
JSON tape-retained parser has no machine-derivation path yet; this is
the source of the false headers. The `json_sink_direct` module
documentation itself flags the retained-path preamble as outside its
scope:

> "A sink-only program carrying a `value` rule is the JSON family —
> `json_sink_direct` keys its recursive-descent dispatch off the
> `value`-Alt."

The preamble's parse functions (`parse_object`, `parse_array`, etc.)
are structurally analogous to what `json_sink_direct` derives for the
sink path. The gap is that no emitter derives them for the tape path.

---

## Retire Paths

The correct disposition for each false-header file is derivation, not
stripping. Stripping the header and keeping the file as a static courier
leaves the violation intact in substance (hand-authored content flowing
through an `include_str!` gap in the IR pipeline). The idiomatic
transposition for each:

**`value.rs`** — `JsonNodeKind` discriminants are the structural byte
alphabet (`b"{}[],:\""`), the number prefix bytes, and the JSON
literal-initial bytes. The alphabet is already present in the
`SinkOnlyProgram` recognizer rules. A `render_value_types()` emitter
inside `json_sink_direct` (or a new sibling `json_tape_types.rs` module)
derives the enum and the `JsonValue` / `JsonToken` structs from the
recognizer shapes. `ParseError` and `ParseErrorKind` are generic tape
artifacts derivable from the program's error surface, already sketched
in `general_descent::render_view()`.

**`view.rs`** — `JsonObject`/`JsonArray`/etc. are cursor-walking
wrappers over the tape. The general-descent emitter at
`codegen/src/general_descent/` already produces analogous view types
for Google Sheets (`render_view()`). The JSON view layer is richer (pair
iteration, `to_canonical_string`), but the structure is identical. A
`render_tape_view()` emission pass over the `SinkOnlyProgram` grammar
rules produces the correct file and removes the static template entirely.

**`generated.rs` preamble** — the tape-retained parse functions
(`parse_json`, `parse_object`, `parse_array`, ...) follow a structural
pattern that `json_sink_direct`'s `SinkWalk` already resolves for the
sink path. The retire path is to extend `SinkWalk` with a `RetainedWalk`
or `TapeWalk` variant that emits the same structural descent with tape
emissions instead of sink calls. Once this emitter exists,
`json_templates/generated.rs` is retired entirely: `emit_sink_only`
calls `retain_walk.render()` for the preamble and appends
`sink_walk.render()` for the direct path.

**`parser.rs`** — `ParserState` is parameterized only by the tape
capacity plan and the structural alphabet (both available from
`SinkOnlyProgram`). This is a five-field struct whose shape is already
implied by `general_descent`'s generated parser state. A
`render_parser_state()` function in `json_sink_direct` or
`runtime_generator.rs` replaces the static template.

---

## Lock 14 Implication

Lock 14 requires zero grammar-specific code in any generic crate. The
four template files do not name JSON explicitly in their crate-level
paths (they live inside `codegen/src/json_templates/` and are keyed
only by the `has_rule("value")` structural dispatch in
`runtime_generator.rs`). The dispatch is shape-based, not name-based.
However, the content of `generated.rs` and `view.rs` contains
JSON-specific type names (`JsonObject`, `JsonString`, etc.) that are
static string literals inside the template rather than parameterized
via the grammar name. The retire path above (grammar-derived view emitter
with a `pascal_prefix` token derived from the grammar name) resolves
both the courier violation and the residual JSON-specificity in the
template strings.

---
